## React Native Development Standards

### New Architecture & Runtime
- Target the **New Architecture** exclusively — Fabric renderer, TurboModules, and JSI are the production standard. **NEVER** write code that depends on the legacy bridge.
- Use **Hermes** as the JavaScript engine — it is required for the New Architecture and provides AOT bytecode compilation for faster startup and lower memory usage.
- Verify all third-party packages support the New Architecture before adoption — check [reactnative.directory](https://reactnative.directory) for compatibility status.
- Migrate custom native modules to **TurboModules** for lazy loading — modules load only when first accessed, reducing app startup time.

### Preferred Folder Hierarchy & Architecture
- `src/app/`: Expo Router file-based routes that define the navigation tree.
- `src/features/{name}/api/`: Feature-specific API calls, query hooks, and mutation handlers.
- `src/features/{name}/components/`: Feature-specific UI components.
- `src/features/{name}/hooks/`: Feature-specific custom hooks.
- `src/features/{name}/types.ts`: Feature-scoped TypeScript interfaces and types.
- `src/components/`: Truly global, reusable UI primitives (Button, Input, Card) — move a component here only when it is used by 3+ unrelated features.
- `src/hooks/`: Global hooks (`useAuth`, `useTheme`, `useNetworkStatus`).
- `src/services/`: Global services (API client configuration, analytics, push notifications).
- `src/utils/`: Pure utility functions with zero side effects.

### Hooks Philosophy
- Treat `useEffect` as a **last resort** — it is for synchronizing with external systems (subscriptions, Keyboard listeners, AppState changes) only.
- **NEVER** use `useEffect` for data fetching — use TanStack Query hooks instead.
- **NEVER** use `useEffect` to derive state from other state — compute derived values during render or use `useMemo`.
- Use `useOptimistic` for instant UI feedback during mutations — show the expected result immediately, roll back on failure.
- Keep state as local as possible — only lift state to a parent or global store when two or more unrelated components need it.

### State Management (Layered Approach)
- Use **TanStack Query** for all server state — API data fetching, caching, background refetching, and optimistic updates. This eliminates manual `isLoading`/`isError` state management.
- Use **Zustand** for global client-side UI state (authentication status, theme, shopping cart, modal visibility). Keep stores minimal and focused.
- Use `useState` and `useReducer` for local component state — **NEVER** elevate local UI state (form inputs, toggles) to a global store.
- **NEVER** put server-fetched data into Zustand or Redux — let TanStack Query own the cache.
- Use **MMKV** for high-performance persistent local storage — it is synchronous and significantly faster than AsyncStorage.

### Component Patterns & Rendering
- Prefer composition through the `children` prop pattern — **NEVER** build component APIs that accept JSX via non-children props when `children` suffices.
- Wrap expensive components with `React.memo` to prevent unnecessary re-renders when parent state changes.
- **NEVER** define inline functions or object literals in JSX props — extract them to `useCallback` and `useMemo` to preserve referential equality.
- Extract reusable logic into custom hooks — **NEVER** duplicate stateful logic across multiple components.
- Use `ErrorBoundary` components to catch and recover from rendering errors — **NEVER** let an uncaught error crash the entire application tree.
- Use `testID` prop on all interactive and key content elements — this enables reliable E2E testing and accessibility tooling.
- Prefer controlled components for form inputs — uncontrolled refs should only be used for imperative focus management.
- Define explicit prop types using TypeScript interfaces — use discriminated unions for component variants to make impossible states unrepresentable.

### Performance
- Use **FlashList** (Shopify) instead of `FlatList` for all scrollable lists — it provides superior memory efficiency and scroll performance.
- Provide `estimatedItemSize` to FlashList and `getItemLayout` to FlatList for fixed-height items — this eliminates expensive on-the-fly measurements.
- Use `useNativeDriver: true` for all property-based `Animated` animations — this offloads work from the JS thread to the native UI thread.
- Use **Reanimated 3+** for gesture-driven and complex animations — it runs entirely on the UI thread with no bridge overhead.
- **NEVER** measure performance in debug mode — always use `--profile` builds. Debug mode adds 2–5x overhead that produces misleading results.
- Minimize JS thread work: avoid synchronous computation during render, defer heavy processing to `InteractionManager.runAfterInteractions`.

### Navigation
- Use **Expo Router** for file-based, declarative routing with automatic deep linking support.
- Organize route files to reflect the user's navigational flow: use route groups like `(authenticated)/` and `(public)/` for layout boundaries.
- Define all route paths as named constants — **NEVER** hardcode path strings in `router.push()` or `<Link>` calls.
- Use **Universal Links** (iOS) and **App Links** (Android) for deep linking — **NEVER** rely solely on custom URL schemes (`myapp://`) which lack fallback if the app is not installed.
- When React Navigation v7 is used instead, centralize the `linking` configuration in a single file — **NEVER** scatter deep link mappings across navigators.

### Testing
- Follow the testing pyramid: ~70% unit tests (Jest), ~20% component tests (React Native Testing Library), ~10% E2E tests (Detox or Maestro).
- Query elements by `testID` or accessibility role/label in component tests — **NEVER** query by raw text content, as copy changes break tests.
- Test component **behavior**, not implementation details — verify what the user sees and does, not internal state transitions.
- Mock native modules that do not exist in the Node.js test environment — configure mocks in `jest.setup.js`.
- Use **Maestro** for rapid E2E test authoring (YAML-based, low setup) or **Detox** for gray-box testing with deep native integration.
- Use snapshot tests sparingly — they detect unintended changes but provide low confidence for correctness.

### Accessibility
- Provide `accessibilityLabel` and `accessibilityRole` on all interactive and informational elements for screen readers.
- Ensure minimum touch target sizes of 48x48dp — use `hitSlop` to expand small visual elements without changing layout.
- Support dynamic text scaling — use relative font sizes and test with large text accessibility settings enabled.
- **MUST** test with VoiceOver (iOS) and TalkBack (Android) for all critical user flows.
